questions.question: Design a multi-floor parking lot system (LLD).
questions.title: Design a Parking Lot — Low-Level Design
questions.direct_answer: Model a parking lot as a `ParkingLot` containing multiple `Floor`s, each containing typed `Spot`s (`COMPACT`, `LARGE`, `EV`, `HANDICAPPED`). On entry, a `SpotAllocator` picks a free spot for the vehicle's category and atomically marks it occupied; a `Ticket` is created with entry time. On exit, a `FeeStrategy` computes the bill using ticket entry/exit times and spot type. Use **interfaces for the variation points** — `SpotAllocator` (nearest, by-floor, EV-priority), `FeeStrategy` (hourly, slabbed, day-pass). Make the spot reservation atomic via `ConcurrentHashMap.compute` or per-floor locks to handle concurrent arrivals. Persist tickets via a `TicketRepository` if state must survive restarts. Keep the design swappable, thread-safe, and testable.

interviewer_intent.testing: Decomposition into entities + interfaces, atomic spot allocation under concurrency, separation of fee policy via Strategy, and extensibility for spot types / pricing models / reservations.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Single god `ParkingLotService`; non-atomic spot reservation (two cars get same spot); deep inheritance for vehicle types; fee logic baked into the lot.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss per-floor partitioning for scalability, EV / handicapped spot priority, reservation extension, and persistence vs in-memory trade-off.

sections.title: Problem Framing
sections.content:
A parking lot system handles vehicles arriving and leaving:

- Vehicles enter through gates, get assigned a spot, receive a ticket.
- On exit, the spot is freed and the bill is computed from the ticket.
- Multiple floors; spots come in different sizes; pricing varies by type and duration.

The interesting design pressure is **concurrency** (multiple gates assigning spots at once) and **extensibility** (new spot types, new fee structures, eventual reservations) — not raw scale. Treat it as a single-instance OO design unless the interviewer pushes you to distribute it.

sections.title: Clarifying Questions
sections.content:
Before any design:

- **Lot shape:** single lot, multiple floors? How many spots roughly?
- **Vehicle types:** bike, car, truck, EV?
- **Spot types:** matched 1:1 with vehicle types, or generic spots that fit anything?
- **Reservations or walk-in only?**
- **Pricing:** flat hourly, slabbed (first 2 hours flat then per-hour), day pass?
- **Multiple entry/exit gates** (concurrent assignment)?
- **Persistence:** restart-safe, or in-memory only for the interview?
- **Payment in scope:** model the API or skip and assume out of scope?

Lock down scope explicitly before drawing classes.

sections.title: Assumptions for This Design
sections.content:
- Single lot, multiple floors.
- Spot types: `COMPACT`, `LARGE`, `EV`, `HANDICAPPED`.
- Vehicle categories: `BIKE`, `CAR`, `TRUCK`, `EV` — each maps to one or more compatible spot types.
- Walk-in only (reservations called out as an extension).
- Pricing: hourly with per-spot-type rates (slabbed pricing called out as an extension).
- Multiple concurrent gates; spot reservation must be atomic.
- In-memory state with a `TicketRepository` interface so persistence can drop in.
- Payment marked out of scope; `unpark` returns a `Receipt` with the amount due.

sections.title: Core Entities and Responsibilities
sections.content:
- **`ParkingLot`** — entry point. Holds floors, allocator, fee strategy, ticket repo. `park(vehicle)`, `unpark(ticket)`.
- **`Floor`** — owns a list of spots. Knows how to find a free spot for a given spot type (delegates to allocator).
- **`Spot`** — one parking position. Type, occupied flag, current vehicle (or null).
- **`Vehicle`** — license plate, category. Category determines which spot types are compatible.
- **`Ticket`** — immutable record of (id, vehicle, spot, entry time).
- **`Receipt`** — immutable record of (ticket, exit time, amount).
- **`SpotAllocator`** (interface) — finds the next available spot across floors. Implementations: `NearestSpotAllocator`, `EvPriorityAllocator`.
- **`FeeStrategy`** (interface) — computes amount for a ticket. Implementations: `HourlyFeeStrategy`, `SlabbedFeeStrategy`.
- **`TicketRepository`** (interface) — saves/loads tickets. In-memory impl for now.

sections.title: Class Diagram
sections.content:
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ParkingLot {
        -List~Floor~ floors
        -SpotAllocator allocator
        -FeeStrategy feeStrategy
        -TicketRepository tickets
        +park(Vehicle) Ticket
        +unpark(Ticket) Receipt
    }
    class Floor {
        -int floorNumber
        -Map~SpotType, List~Spot~~ spotsByType
        +findFree(SpotType) Optional~Spot~
    }
    class Spot {
        -SpotId id
        -SpotType type
        -AtomicReference~Vehicle~ occupant
        +tryAssign(Vehicle) bool
        +release()
    }
    class Vehicle {
        -String plate
        -VehicleCategory category
    }
    class Ticket {
        -TicketId id
        -Vehicle vehicle
        -Spot spot
        -Instant entryTime
    }
    class Receipt {
        -Ticket ticket
        -Instant exitTime
        -Money amount
    }
    class SpotAllocator {
        <<interface>>
        +allocate(List~Floor~, Vehicle) Optional~Spot~
    }
    class FeeStrategy {
        <<interface>>
        +calculate(Ticket, Instant) Money
    }
    class TicketRepository {
        <<interface>>
        +save(Ticket)
        +findById(TicketId) Optional~Ticket~
        +remove(TicketId)
    }

    ParkingLot --> Floor
    ParkingLot --> SpotAllocator
    ParkingLot --> FeeStrategy
    ParkingLot --> TicketRepository
    Floor --> Spot
    Spot --> Vehicle
    Ticket --> Spot
    Ticket --> Vehicle
    Receipt --> Ticket
    NearestSpotAllocator ..|> SpotAllocator
    EvPriorityAllocator ..|> SpotAllocator
    HourlyFeeStrategy ..|> FeeStrategy
    SlabbedFeeStrategy ..|> FeeStrategy
    InMemoryTicketRepository ..|> TicketRepository
```

Vehicle category → compatible spot types is captured by a small lookup table in `Vehicle` or in `SpotType.compatibleWith(VehicleCategory)`.

sections.title: Atomic Spot Reservation
Code — Lot, Allocator, Fee Strategy
End-to-End Flow
sections.content:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant V as Vehicle
    participant G as EntryGate
    participant L as ParkingLot
    participant A as SpotAllocator
    participant S as Spot
    participant R as TicketRepository

    V->>G: arrives
    G->>L: park(vehicle)
    L->>A: allocate(floors, vehicle)
    A->>S: tryAssign(vehicle) [CAS]
    S-->>A: true
    A-->>L: Spot
    L->>R: save(ticket)
    L-->>G: Ticket
    G-->>V: hands ticket

    Note over V,L: ... time passes ...

    V->>G: presents ticket at exit
    G->>L: unpark(ticketId)
    L->>R: findById
    L->>L: feeStrategy.calculate(ticket, now)
    L->>S: release()
    L->>R: remove(ticketId)
    L-->>G: Receipt
```

sections.title: Extensibility — Where Future Change Lands
sections.content:
- **New spot type** → add to `SpotType` enum + `SpotType.compatibleWith()` mapping. Allocator/fee strategy untouched.
- **New pricing model** → new `FeeStrategy` implementation (slabbed, day-pass, surge). Configure at construction; no edits elsewhere.
- **New allocation policy** → new `SpotAllocator` (e.g., `EvPriorityAllocator` that prefers EV charging spots for EVs, then falls back). Lot wiring picks one.
- **Reservations** → add a `ReservationService` that holds spots with TTL. `park()` first checks for an active reservation matching the vehicle; otherwise normal allocation.
- **Multi-lot / multi-region** → introduce a `LotDirectory` that picks a lot; lot-level logic unchanged.
- **Persistence** → `JpaTicketRepository` implements `TicketRepository`; spots persisted to DB with optimistic lock.
- **Notifications** → publish `SpotAssignedEvent` / `SpotReleasedEvent`; subscribers update displays / metrics.

sections.title: Failure Modes and Edge Cases
sections.content:
- **Lost ticket:** model `LostTicketPolicy` — charges max-day rate or requires plate verification; another `FeeStrategy` variant or a separate path.
- **Lot full:** `LotFullException` — surface to caller; gate displays 'Full'.
- **Concurrent unpark on the same ticket:** `tickets.remove(id)` should return whether removal succeeded; if not, treat as already exited (idempotent).
- **Crash mid-park:** ticket saved but receipt issuance fails. On retry, ticket already exists — use idempotency key on `park` (vehicle plate + entry minute) so duplicate calls return the same ticket.
- **Spot stuck occupied** (vehicle drove off without paying): nightly reconciliation job that flags spots occupied beyond max stay duration; manual override.
- **Time skew:** all entry/exit times come from a single `Clock`; centralized rather than each spot reading `Instant.now()`.

sections.title: Trade-offs and Alternatives
sections.content:
- **In-memory vs persistent:** in-memory is simpler and faster but loses state on restart. Persistent (Postgres) survives crash but adds latency per park/unpark. Choice driven by 'how bad is losing 30 seconds of parking state?'.
- **Per-spot CAS vs per-floor lock:** CAS is lock-free and scales better; per-floor lock is simpler to reason about but serializes assignments on a floor.
- **Strategy vs rule engine for fees:** Strategy interface is enough for 5-10 pricing variants. A rule engine (Drools) is overkill until tariffs become genuinely customer-configurable.
- **Inheritance for vehicle types:** avoid. `VehicleCategory` enum + `compatibleWith` mapping is enough. A subclass per vehicle type buys nothing.
- **Distributed coordination:** if multiple lot instances must share state, move state to Redis (`SET NX` for spot locks, sorted set for tickets). Adds operational complexity; only justified for a multi-region operator.

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **Entities:** `ParkingLot`, `Floor`, `Spot`, `Vehicle`, `Ticket`, `Receipt`.
- **Variation behind interfaces:** `SpotAllocator`, `FeeStrategy`, `TicketRepository`.
- **Atomic spot assignment** via `AtomicReference.compareAndSet` — lock-free per spot.
- **`Clock` injection** for testability.
- **Composition over inheritance** — `VehicleCategory` enum + compatibility table; no `Car extends Vehicle`.
- **Extension points wired** for reservations, multi-lot, persistence, notifications.
- **Idempotency** on park to survive retries; nightly reconciliation for stuck spots.
- **Walk-in default;** reservations are an explicit extension.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**Problem framing**

Vehicles arrive at gates, get assigned a spot, receive a ticket. On exit, spot freed and bill computed. Multiple floors; spots come in different sizes; pricing varies. Design pressure is concurrency (multiple gates) and extensibility (new spot types, fee structures, reservations) — not raw scale.

**Clarifying questions**

Lot shape (single, multiple floors, count). Vehicle types. Spot types matched 1:1 or generic. Reservations or walk-in. Pricing (flat hourly, slabbed, day pass). Multiple gates. Persistence. Payment in scope.

**Assumptions**

Single lot, multiple floors. Spot types COMPACT/LARGE/EV/HANDICAPPED. Vehicle categories BIKE/CAR/TRUCK/EV — each maps to compatible spot types. Walk-in (reservations as extension). Hourly pricing per spot type (slabbed as extension). Multiple concurrent gates; atomic reservation. In-memory state with TicketRepository interface for future persistence. Payment out of scope; unpark returns Receipt with amount due.

**Core entities**

ParkingLot: entry point, holds floors, allocator, fee strategy, ticket repo. park(vehicle), unpark(ticket).
Floor: owns list of spots, finds free spot for a type.
Spot: one parking position. Type, occupied flag, current vehicle.
Vehicle: license plate, category. Category determines compatible spot types.
Ticket: immutable record (id, vehicle, spot, entry time).
Receipt: immutable record (ticket, exit time, amount).
SpotAllocator interface: NearestSpotAllocator, EvPriorityAllocator.
FeeStrategy interface: HourlyFeeStrategy, SlabbedFeeStrategy.
TicketRepository interface: in-memory impl for now.

**Atomic spot reservation**

Two cars at two gates must not get same spot.

Per-spot atomic check-and-set (recommended): Spot has AtomicReference<Vehicle> occupant. tryAssign(v) calls occupant.compareAndSet(null, v). Allocator iterates candidate spots; first one whose tryAssign returns true wins. Lock-free per spot.

Alternatives: per-floor synchronized lock (simpler, serializes assignments per floor). Distributed Redis SET NX (for cross-instance, mention only if asked about distribution).

**Code — lot, allocator, fee strategy**

ParkingLot.park(v): allocator.allocate(floors, v) or throw LotFullException. Create Ticket with TicketId.next(), v, spot, clock.instant(). tickets.save(t). Return t.

ParkingLot.unpark(id): tickets.findById, throw InvalidTicketException if missing. exit = clock.instant(). amount = feeStrategy.calculate(t, exit). t.spot().release(). tickets.remove(id). Return new Receipt.

NearestSpotAllocator: iterate floors (ordered by proximity), iterate compatible SpotTypes for vehicle category, findFree on each floor, tryAssign. First successful CAS wins.

HourlyFeeStrategy: minutes between entry and exit, round up to hours, minimum charge of 1 hour, multiply hourlyRates[spot.type] by hours.

Clock injection — testable without freezing real time.

**End-to-end flow**

Vehicle arrives → EntryGate calls park(vehicle) → Lot calls allocator.allocate → spot.tryAssign (CAS) → lot creates ticket → saves → returns to gate → vehicle gets ticket. Time passes. Vehicle presents ticket → unpark(ticketId) → findById → feeStrategy.calculate → spot.release → remove ticket → Receipt.

**Extensibility**

- New spot type → add to enum + compatibleWith mapping; allocator/fee untouched
- New pricing → new FeeStrategy impl; configure at construction
- New allocation policy → new SpotAllocator (EvPriorityAllocator); lot wiring picks one
- Reservations → ReservationService holds spots with TTL; park() checks active reservation matching vehicle first
- Multi-lot → LotDirectory picks a lot; lot-level logic unchanged
- Persistence → JpaTicketRepository implements interface; spots persisted with optimistic lock
- Notifications → publish SpotAssignedEvent / SpotReleasedEvent; subscribers update displays/metrics

**Failure modes**

- Lost ticket: LostTicketPolicy — max-day rate or plate verification
- Lot full: LotFullException; gate displays 'Full'
- Concurrent unpark on same ticket: tickets.remove returns whether succeeded; idempotent
- Crash mid-park: ticket saved but receipt fails. Idempotency key on park (plate + entry minute); duplicate calls return same ticket
- Spot stuck occupied: nightly reconciliation job; flags spots beyond max stay duration; manual override
- Time skew: all entry/exit from single Clock; centralized

**Trade-offs and alternatives**

- In-memory vs persistent: in-memory simpler/faster but loses state on restart; persistent survives crash with latency cost. Driven by tolerance for losing seconds of state
- Per-spot CAS vs per-floor lock: CAS scales better; per-floor lock simpler but serializes per floor
- Strategy vs rule engine for fees: Strategy enough for 5-10 variants; rule engine (Drools) overkill until customer-configurable tariffs
- Inheritance for vehicle types: avoid; enum + compatibility table
- Distributed coordination: Redis SET NX for multi-instance; only for multi-region operator

**Recommendation**

**Build a single ParkingLot aggregating typed Floors and Spots, with SpotAllocator and FeeStrategy as interfaces so allocation policy and pricing are swappable. Make spot assignment lock-free using AtomicReference + compareAndSet on each Spot, so concurrent gates can't double-book. Inject Clock and TicketRepository for testability and future persistence. Use enum + compatibility mapping for vehicle/spot types instead of inheritance hierarchies. Reservations, persistence, and multi-lot are clear extensions that drop in without touching the core flow.**

What changes if you have to support thousands of lots across regions from a single API?
How do you handle a lost ticket cleanly without bolting it onto the fee strategy?
Walk through how `Spot.tryAssign` prevents two cars from being assigned the same spot.
